name: Act of March 3, 1873 (deficiency appropriations): purchase of a White Earth township for the Pembina band of Chippewa
citation: Act of March 3, 1873, ch. 228, 17 Stat. 530, at 539
nations: Pembina band of Chippewa (Ojibwe), whose descendants are in the Red Lake, White Earth and Turtle Mountain bands
Mississippi bands of Chippewa (Ojibwe), sellers of the township
promises: Congress appropriated up to $25,000 to buy from the Mississippi bands of Chippewa one township of land in the White Earth reservation in Minnesota, for the use and benefit of the Pembina band.
Congress appropriated up to $10,000 to aid and assist the Pembina band in establishing themselves on the White Earth reservation.
today: Royce (1899) records that the township was bought under this act and that T. 144 N., R. 42 W. was selected for the purpose by Special Agent Luce on February 14, 1883.

sources.title: Act of March 3, 1873, ch. 228 (deficiency appropriations), 17 Stat. 530, page 539
Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule entry 542

openQuestions: treaties.json names the Pembina band as the tribe for this cession, but the act buys the township from the Mississippi bands of Chippewa for the Pembina; the Pembina received land here rather than giving it up.
Royce records that the township was only selected in February 1883, ten years after the act; whether the $10,000 for establishing the band was spent, and why selection took ten years, was not traced.

The Pembina band's own claims (Indian Claims Commission Dockets 18-A, 113 and others) concern the 1863 Old Crossing treaty and later agreements, not this act; they were not reviewed for this file. The later loss of White Earth land under the 1889 Nelson Act belongs to other files.
No account by the Turtle Mountain, Red Lake or White Earth bands of this purchase was found.
